name: Utility feed and on-site substation for data centres
applications: Voltage transformation from transmission to data hall distribution
Redundancy design (N+1 feeds, dual redundant substations)
principle: A hyperscale campus is a utility-scale load: the feed is taken at transmission or high distribution voltage and transformed on site, because the alternative is carrying tens of megawatts at utilisation voltage. The binding constraint is less often transformer capacity than the interconnection queue and the local network's ability to absorb a step load, which the IEA flags as a first-order constraint in its high-growth case.

process_steps.name: Interconnection request and utility study define the deliverable capacity
Transmission or HV distribution line is terminated at the site substation
Power transformers step down to the site distribution voltage
MV switchgear distributes to data hall substations and UPS plant

key_equipment: metering at the point of supply

performance.metric: global electricity generation to supply data centres, 2024
performance.basis: IEA: global electricity generation to supply data centres grows from 460 TWh in 2024 to over 1000 TWh in 2030 and 1300 TWh in 2035 in the base case; data centres rise from about 1 percent of global electricity generation today to 3 percent in 2030.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy supply for AI, read 2026-11-14

performance.metric: share of additional data centre demand met by renewables over five years
performance.basis: IEA: over five years renewables meet nearly half of the additional demand, followed by gas and coal.

source.note: IEA, Energy and AI, Energy supply for AI, read 2026-11-14

advantages: Allows a campus to be sized in tens to hundreds of megawatts
On-site transformation keeps distribution at a practical voltage
Dual feeds and redundant substations support concurrent maintainability
limitations: Interconnection queues can delay a project by years in constrained networks
Substation lead times for large power transformers are long
Step loads and harmonics need utility agreement, not just equipment
